sanskrit: ākarṣas te 'vākphalaḥ kupraṇīto; hṛdi prauḍho mantrapadaḥ samādhiḥ yudhiṣṭhireṇa saphalaḥ saṃstavo 'stu; sāmnaḥ surikto 'rimateḥ sudhanvā
english: Your dice-throw is ill-led and yields downward fruit; the counsel deep-seated in your heart is firm resolve. May the agreement with Yudhiṣṭhira prove fruitful; well-spoken is the conciliation of the enemy-tamer, the skilled archer Sudhanvan.

sanskrit: prātipīyāḥ śāṃtanavāś ca rājan; kāvyāṃ vācaṃ śṛṇuta mātyagād vaḥ vaiśvānaraṃ prajvalitaṃ sughoram; ayuddhena praśamayatotpatantam
english: O king, you descendants of Pratīpa and of Shantanu, hear this counsel-laden speech — do not let it pass you by. The blazing, terrible fire of Vaiśvānara has flared up; quench this rising flame without resort to battle.

sanskrit: yadā manyuṃ pāṇḍavo 'jātaśatrur; na saṃyacched akṣamayābhibhūtaḥ vṛkodaraḥ savyasācī yamau ca; ko 'tra dvīpaḥ syāt tumule vas tadānīm
english: When Yudhiṣṭhira, Ajātaśatru among the Pāṇḍavas, overwhelmed by intolerable provocation, can no longer restrain his wrath — and when Vṛkodara, Savyasācī, and the twin sons of Mādrī are unleashed — what refuge will there then be for you in that tumult?

sanskrit: mahārāja prabhavas tvaṃ dhanānāṃ; purā dyūtān manasā yāvad iccheḥ bahu vittaṃ pāṇḍavāṃś cej jayes tvaṃ; kiṃ tena syād vasu vindeha pārthān
english: O great king, you are master of all wealth; before this gambling began you could take in your mind as much as you desired. Even if you were to win great riches by defeating the Pāṇḍavas in dice, what good would that wealth be? Find your treasure in the sons of Pṛthā instead.

sanskrit: jānīmahe devitaṃ saubalasya; veda dyūte nikṛtiṃ pārvatīyaḥ yataḥ prāptaḥ śakunis tatra yātu; māyāyodhī bhārata pārvatīyaḥ
english: We know well the gambling of Subala's son; the mountain-born one understands the deceit of the dice. Let Śakuni return to the land from which he came — that fighter with illusion, that hill-man, O Bharata.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca pareṣām eva yaśasā ślāghase tvaṃ; sadā channaḥ kutsayan dhārtarāṣṭrān jānīmas tvāṃ vidura yatpriyas tvaṃ; bālān ivāsmān avamanyase tvam
english: Duryodhana said: You boast only of the glory of others; ever concealed, you revile the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. We know you, Vidura, and to whom your heart belongs — you despise us as if we were children.

sanskrit: suvijñeyaḥ puruṣo 'nyatrakāmo; nindāpraśaṃse hi tathā yunakti jihvā manas te hṛdayaṃ nirvyanakti; jyāyo nirāha manasaḥ prātikūlyam
english: A man whose affections lie elsewhere is easily known, for he directs his censure and his praise accordingly. Your tongue, Vidura, betrays your heart and lays it bare; it declares plainly the mind's own opposition.

sanskrit: utsaṅgena vyāla ivāhṛto 'si; mārjāravat poṣakaṃ copahaṃsi bhartṛghnatvān na hi pāpīya āhus; tasmāt kṣattaḥ kiṃ na bibheṣi pāpāt
english: You have been raised in our lap like a serpent; like a cat you harm the very one who nourishes you. They say there is no greater sin than the betrayal of one's master — so why, O Kṣattā, do you not fear that sin?

sanskrit: jitvā śatrūn phalam āptaṃ mahan no; māsmān kṣattaḥ paruṣāṇīha vocaḥ dviṣadbhis tvaṃ saṃprayogābhinandī; muhur dveṣaṃ yāsi naḥ saṃpramohāt
english: We have conquered our enemies and obtained a great prize — do not, O Kṣattā, speak harsh words to us here. You rejoice in association with our foes and through bewilderment you turn again and again toward enmity with us.

sanskrit: amitratāṃ yāti naro 'kṣamaṃ bruvan; nigūhate guhyam amitrasaṃstave tadāśritāpatrapā kiṃ na bādhate; yad icchasi tvaṃ tad ihādya bhāṣase
english: A man who speaks what is intolerable creates enmity for himself; he hides his secrets while praising enemies. Does not the shame of the refuge you have taken weigh upon you? Today you speak here whatever you desire.

sanskrit: mā no 'vamaṃsthā vidma manas tavedaṃ; śikṣasva buddhiṃ sthavirāṇāṃ sakāśāt yaśo rakṣasva vidura saṃpraṇītaṃ; mā vyāpṛtaḥ parakāryeṣu bhūs tvam
english: Do not insult us — we know the mind that is in you. Go and learn wisdom from the assembly of elders. Guard the reputation of this house, O Vidura, as it has been upheld — do not busy yourself in the affairs of others.

sanskrit: ahaṃ karteti vidura māvamaṃsthā; mā no nityaṃ paruṣāṇīha vocaḥ na tvāṃ pṛcchāmi vidura yad dhitaṃ me; svasti kṣattar mā titikṣūn kṣiṇu tvam
english: Do not insult us with "I am the one who acts", O Vidura; do not speak harsh words to us constantly here. I do not ask you, Vidura, for what is beneficial to me. Farewell, O Kṣattā — do not go on tormenting those who endure in patience.

sanskrit: ekaḥ śāstā na dvitīyo 'sti śāstā; garbhe śayānaṃ puruṣaṃ śāsti śāstā tenānuśiṣṭaḥ pravaṇād ivāmbho; yathā niyukto 'smi tathā vahāmi
english: There is one ordainer; there is no second ordainer. That ordainer directs a man even as he lies in the womb. Instructed by that one, I flow as water follows a downward slope — I carry forward exactly as I have been appointed.

sanskrit: bhinatti śirasā śailam ahiṃ bhojayate ca yaḥ sa eva tasya kurute kāryāṇām anuśāsanam
english: He who shatters a mountain with his head and feeds a serpent — that same power alone governs the ordering of his actions.

sanskrit: yo balād anuśāstīha so 'mitraṃ tena vindati mitratām anuvṛttaṃ tu samupekṣeta paṇḍitaḥ
english: One who imposes his counsel by force here becomes an enemy by that very act; but a wise man should overlook compliant, submissive conduct.

sanskrit: pradīpya yaḥ pradīptāgniṃ prāk tvaran nābhidhāvati bhasmāpi na sa vindeta śiṣṭaṃ kva cana bhārata
english: He who has kindled a blazing fire and does not run quickly toward it in time — even ashes he will not find remaining anywhere, O Bharata.

sanskrit: na vāsayet pāravargyaṃ dviṣantaṃ; viśeṣataḥ kṣattar ahitaṃ manuṣyam sa yatrecchasi vidura tatra gaccha; susāntvitāpi hy asatī strī jahāti
english: One should not harbor in one's house an enemy, especially an ill-wishing person, O Kṣattā. Go wherever you wish, Vidura — for even a faithless woman, however well appeased, will in the end abandon her lord.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca etāvatā ye puruṣaṃ tyajanti; teṣāṃ sakhyam antavad brūhi rājan rājñāṃ hi cittāni pariplutāni; sāntvaṃ dattvā musalair ghātayanti
english: Vidura said: Those who abandon a man for so little — declare their friendship to be of short duration, O king. For the minds of kings are turbulent; they give gentle words and then strike with clubs.

sanskrit: abālas tvaṃ manyase rājaputra; bālo 'ham ity eva sumandabuddhe yaḥ sauhṛde puruṣaṃ sthāpayitvā; paścād enaṃ dūṣayate sa bālaḥ
english: You consider yourself not a child, O prince; and I too regard myself as no child, O you of very dull understanding. He who first establishes a man in friendship and afterwards defames him — that one is the true child.

sanskrit: na śreyase nīyate mandabuddhiḥ; strī śrotriyasyeva gṛhe praduṣṭā dhruvaṃ na roced bharatarṣabhasya; patiḥ kumāryā iva ṣaṣṭivarṣaḥ
english: A dull-witted man is not led toward the good — like a corrupt woman in the house of a learned brahmin. He will surely not please the bull of the Bharatas — as a husband of sixty years cannot please a young maiden.

sanskrit: anupriyaṃ ced anukāṅkṣase tvaṃ; sarveṣu kāryeṣu hitāhiteṣu striyaś ca rājañ jaḍapaṅgukāṃś ca; pṛccha tvaṃ vai tādṛśāṃś caiva mūḍhān
english: If you desire only pleasant words in all matters, both beneficial and harmful, then, O king, ask women and the dull and the lame and fools of that sort.

sanskrit: labhyaḥ khalu prātipīya naro 'nupriyavāg iha apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ
english: Indeed, O descendant of Pratīpa, a man who speaks only pleasant words is easily found in this world; but one who speaks what is unpleasant yet wholesome, and one who listens to such counsel, is rare.

sanskrit: yas tu dharme parāśvasya hitvā bhartuḥ priyāpriye apriyāṇy āha pathyāni tena rājā sahāyavān
english: But he who, resting on righteousness and setting aside alike what pleases and displeases his lord, speaks what is unpleasant yet salutary — by that one a king is truly assisted.

sanskrit: avyādhijaṃ kaṭukaṃ tīkṣṇam uṣṇaṃ; yaśomuṣaṃ paruṣaṃ pūtigandhi satāṃ peyaṃ yan na pibanty asanto; manyuṃ mahārāja piba praśāmya
english: What the good must drink but the wicked will not — that which is bitter though not born of disease, sharp, burning, robbing one of glory, harsh, and ill-smelling — drink down your wrath, O great king, and be pacified.

sanskrit: vaicitravīryasya yaśo dhanaṃ ca; vāñchāmy ahaṃ sahaputrasya śaśvat yathā tathā vo 'stu namaś ca vo 'stu; mamāpi ca svasti diśantu viprāḥ
english: I wish always for the glory and the wealth of Vicitravīrya's line, together with his sons. May it be so for you in whatever way it shall be; and my reverence too is yours. May the brahmins also grant well-being to me.

sanskrit: āśīviṣān netraviṣān kopayen na tu paṇḍitaḥ evaṃ te 'haṃ vadāmīdaṃ prayataḥ kurunandana
english: A wise man should not provoke those who carry venom in their fangs, or those who carry venom in their gaze. This is what I tell you now with care, O joy of the Kuru race.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca bahu vittaṃ parājaiṣīḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira ācakṣva vittaṃ kaunteya yadi te 'sty aparājitam
english: Śakuni said: You have lost much wealth of the Pāṇḍavas, Yudhiṣṭhira. Declare what wealth remains, O son of Kuntī, if any you possess that is not yet lost.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mama vittam asaṃkhyeyaṃ yad ahaṃ veda saubala atha tvaṃ śakune kasmād vittaṃ samanupṛcchasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: My wealth is beyond counting, as I myself know, O son of Subala. But why do you ask about wealth, O Śakuni?

sanskrit: ayutaṃ prayutaṃ caiva kharvaṃ padmaṃ tathārbudam śaṅkhaṃ caiva nikharvaṃ ca samudraṃ cātra paṇyatām etan mama dhanaṃ rājaṃs tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Ten thousand, a million, a kharva, a padma, an arbuda, a shankha, a nikharva, and a samudra — let these be set as stake. This is my wealth, O king; with it I play against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca gavāśvaṃ bahudhenūkam asaṃkhyeyam ajāvikam yat kiṃ cid anuvarṇānāṃ prāk sindhor api saubala etan mama dhanaṃ rājaṃs tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: My cattle and horses, my countless cows and milch-animals, my sheep and goats, and whatever belongs to the peoples of all varnas this side of the Sindhu, O son of Subala — this is my wealth, O king; with it I play against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca puraṃ janapado bhūmir abrāhmaṇadhanaiḥ saha abrāhmaṇāś ca puruṣā rājañ śiṣṭaṃ dhanaṃ mama etad rājan dhanaṃ mahyaṃ tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The city, the realm, the land, together with the wealth of those who are not brahmins, and all persons of non-brahmin birth — O king, this is the remaining wealth that is mine. With this, O king, I play against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rājaputrā ime rājañ śobhante yena bhūṣitāḥ kuṇḍalāni ca niṣkāś ca sarvaṃ cāṅgavibhūṣaṇam etan mama dhanaṃ rājaṃs tena dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: These princes, O king, shine with their adornments — their earrings and gold necklaces and all their bodily ornaments. This is my wealth, O king; with it I play against you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca śyāmo yuvā lohitākṣaḥ siṃhaskandho mahābhujaḥ nakulo glaha eko me yac caitat svagataṃ dhanam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Dark, young, with reddish eyes, lion-shouldered, great-armed — Nakula is my one stake, along with whatever wealth of mine belongs to him personally.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca priyas te nakulo rājan rājaputro yudhiṣṭhira asmākaṃ dhanatāṃ prāpto bhūyas tvaṃ kena dīvyasi
english: Śakuni said: Nakula is dear to you, O king, O prince Yudhiṣṭhira — he has now become our property. What now will you stake next?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tu śakunis tān akṣān pratyapadyata jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, Śakuni took those dice in hand; and said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ayaṃ dharmān sahadevo 'nuśāsti; loke hy asmin paṇḍitākhyāṃ gataś ca anarhatā rājaputreṇa tena; tvayā dīvyāmy apriyavat priyeṇa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This Sahadeva who instructs in dharma and has attained the name of wise man in this world — though he does not deserve to be staked — with that beloved prince I play against you, even though it is against my will.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca mādrīputrau priyau rājaṃs tavemau vijitau mayā garīyāṃsau tu te manye bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau
english: Śakuni said: These two sons of Mādrī, O king, are dear to you — both have been won by me. But I think the weightier stakes are Bhīmasena and Dhanañjaya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca adharmaṃ carase nūnaṃ yo nāvekṣasi vai nayam yo naḥ sumanasāṃ mūḍha vibhedaṃ kartum icchasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: You surely walk the path of unrighteousness, you who take no heed of right conduct — you who desire, O fool, to sow division among us who are of one mind.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca garte mattaḥ prapatati pramattaḥ sthāṇum ṛcchati jyeṣṭho rājan variṣṭho 'si namas te bharatarṣabha
english: Śakuni said: One who is intoxicated falls into a pit; one who is heedless stumbles into a post. You are the eldest, O king, the most venerable — my salutation to you, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: svapne na tāni paśyanti jāgrato vā yudhiṣṭhira kitavā yāni dīvyantaḥ pralapanty utkaṭā iva
english: Gamblers do not see those things in dream or waking, O Yudhiṣṭhira, of which they babble wildly while playing their dice — raving like the intoxicated.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yo naḥ saṃkhye naur iva pāranetā; jetā ripūṇāṃ rājaputras tarasvī anarhatā lokavīreṇa tena; dīvyāmy ahaṃ śakune phalgunena
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: He who leads us in battle like a boat to the farther shore — that swift royal prince, conqueror of enemies — though he does not deserve to be staked, with that hero of the world, with Phalguna, I play against you, O Śakuni.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca ayaṃ mayā pāṇḍavānāṃ dhanurdharaḥ; parājitaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ savyasācī bhīmena rājan dayitena dīvya; yat kaitavyaṃ pāṇḍava te 'vaśiṣṭam
english: Śakuni said: This bowman of the Pāṇḍavas — Savyasācī the Pāṇḍava — has been defeated by me. Now stake your beloved Bhīma, O king; stake whatever remains to be staked, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yo no netā yo yudhāṃ naḥ praṇetā; yathā vajrī dānavaśatrur ekaḥ tiryakprekṣī saṃhatabhrūr mahātmā; siṃhaskandho yaś ca sadātyamarṣī
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: He who is our leader, who leads us in battle like the Thunderbolt-bearer who is the sole foe of the demons — he of the sidelong glance, with joined eyebrows, great-souled, lion-shouldered, and ever beyond endurance of insult —

sanskrit: balena tulyo yasya pumān na vidyate; gadābhṛtām agrya ihārimardanaḥ anarhatā rājaputreṇa tena; dīvyāmy ahaṃ bhīmasenena rājan
english: — he whose equal in strength no man exists, the foremost among mace-wielders here, the crusher of enemies — though he does not deserve to be staked, with that royal prince Bhīmasena I play against you, O king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca bahu vittaṃ parājaiṣīr bhrātṝṃś ca sahayadvipān ācakṣva vittaṃ kaunteya yadi te 'sty aparājitam
english: Śakuni said: You have lost great wealth, and your brothers along with their elephants. Declare what wealth remains, O son of Kuntī, if any you possess that is not yet lost.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ahaṃ viśiṣṭaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ dayitas tathā kuryāmas te jitāḥ karma svayam ātmany upaplave
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I am the foremost of all my brothers and equally their beloved. Now that my brothers are lost and our own calamity has fallen upon me, I stake myself.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā vyavasito nikṛtiṃ samupāśritaḥ jitam ity eva śakunir yudhiṣṭhiram abhāṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, Śakuni, resolved and resorting to his deceit, said to Yudhiṣṭhira: "Won."

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca etat pāpiṣṭham akaror yad ātmānaṃ parājitaḥ śiṣṭe sati dhane rājan pāpa ātmaparājayaḥ
english: Śakuni said: This was the most sinful act you have done — staking yourself when you had already lost your brothers and while wealth still remained. O king, the staking of oneself is indeed sin.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā matākṣas tān glahe sarvān avasthitān parājayal lokavīrān ākṣepeṇa pṛthak pṛthak
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the shrewd dice-player, by his casting, defeated separately, one by one, those world-heroes who stood as stakes in the game.

sanskrit: śakunir uvāca asti vai te priyā devī glaha eko 'parājitaḥ paṇasva kṛṣṇāṃ pāñcālīṃ tayātmānaṃ punar jaya
english: Śakuni said: There is indeed your beloved queen — one stake not yet lost. Stake Kṛṣṇā, the Pāñcālī princess; with her win yourself back.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca naiva hrasvā na mahatī nātikṛṣṇā na rohiṇī sarāgaraktanetrā ca tayā dīvyāmy ahaṃ tvayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: She is neither too short nor too tall, neither too dark nor too fair, with eyes tinged with passionate red — with her I play against you.

sanskrit: śāradotpalapatrākṣyā śāradotpalagandhayā śāradotpalasevinyā rūpeṇa śrīsamānayā
english: Her eyes are like the petals of the autumnal lotus; her fragrance is that of the autumnal lotus; she is attended upon like the autumnal lotus; in beauty she is equal to Śrī herself.

sanskrit: tathaiva syād ānṛśaṃsyāt tathā syād rūpasaṃpadā tathā syāc chīlasaṃpattyā yām icchet puruṣaḥ striyam
english: And further she has compassion, beauty of form, and excellence of character — all the qualities for which a man could desire a woman.

sanskrit: caramaṃ saṃviśati yā prathamaṃ pratibudhyate ā gopālāvipālebhyaḥ sarvaṃ veda kṛtākṛtam
english: She who retires last and wakes first, who knows everything done and undone, from the cowherds to the shepherds — that woman I stake.

sanskrit: ābhāti padmavad vaktraṃ sasvedaṃ mallikeva ca vedīmadhyā dīrghakeśī tāmrākṣī nātiromaśā
english: Her face shines like a lotus even when lightly perspiring, and like jasmine. Her waist is slender as an altar, her hair long, her eyes copper-red, and her body not overly covered with hair.

sanskrit: tayaivaṃvidhayā rājan pāñcālyāhaṃ sumadhyayā glahaṃ dīvyāmi cārvaṅgyā draupadyā hanta saubala
english: With her, thus endowed, O king — with the Pāñcālī Draupadī, she of the beautiful slender waist and lovely limbs — I play the dice, O Subala's son.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukte tu vacane dharmarājena bhārata dhig dhig ity eva vṛddhānāṃ sabhyānāṃ niḥsṛtā giraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the king of dharma spoke these words, O Bharata, the voices of the elder assembly members burst forth with cries of "Shame! Shame!"

sanskrit: cukṣubhe sā sabhā rājan rājñāṃ saṃjajñire kathāḥ bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādīnāṃ svedaś ca samajāyata
english: That assembly was convulsed, O king; conversations broke out among the kings, and sweat broke out upon Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and the others.

sanskrit: śiro gṛhītvā viduro gatasattva ivābhavat āste dhyāyann adhovaktro niḥśvasan pannago yathā
english: Vidura clasped his head and became as if bereft of his senses; he sat absorbed in thought, his face cast downward, sighing like a serpent.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭras tu saṃhṛṣṭaḥ paryapṛcchat punaḥ punaḥ kiṃ jitaṃ kiṃ jitam iti hy ākāraṃ nābhyarakṣata
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, filled with delight, asked again and again: "What is won? What is won?" — he could not conceal the expression on his face.

sanskrit: jaharṣa karṇo 'tibhṛśaṃ saha duḥśāsanādibhiḥ itareṣāṃ tu sabhyānāṃ netrebhyaḥ prāpataj jalam
english: Karṇa rejoiced exceedingly along with Duḥśāsana and the others; from the eyes of the remaining assembly members tears fell down.

sanskrit: saubalas tv avicāryaiva jitakāśī madotkaṭaḥ jitam ity eva tān akṣān punar evānvapadyata
english: But the son of Subala, without deliberating, exultant in victory, arrogant with elation, took up those dice once more with the cry: "Won!"

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca ehi kṣattar draupadīm ānayasva; priyāṃ bhāryāṃ saṃmatāṃ pāṇḍavānām saṃmārjatāṃ veśma paraitu śīghram; ānando naḥ saha dāsībhir astu
english: Duryodhana said: Come, O Kṣattā — bring Draupadī here, the beloved wife honoured by the Pāṇḍavas. Let her quickly come to sweep out the household; let there be joy for us together with our maidservants.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca durvibhāvyaṃ bhavati tvādṛśena; na manda saṃbudhyasi pāśabaddhaḥ prapāte tvaṃ lambamāno na vetsi; vyāghrān mṛgaḥ kopayase 'tibālyāt
english: Vidura said: What is about to happen is hard to conceive by one like you, O fool — you do not understand, bound as you are in the noose of fate, hanging over the precipice. Like a deer you are provoking tigers out of sheer childishness.

sanskrit: āśīviṣāḥ śirasi te pūrṇakośā mahāviṣāḥ mā kopiṣṭhāḥ sumandātman mā gamas tvaṃ yamakṣayam
english: Deadly serpents, their poison sacs full, swollen with great venom, rest upon your head. Do not provoke them, O extremely foolish one — do not walk toward the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: na hi dāsītvam āpannā kṛṣṇā bhavati bhārata anīśena hi rājñaiṣā paṇe nyasteti me matiḥ
english: Kṛṣṇā does not become a slave in this manner, O Bharata — for it is my judgment that this queen was staked as a wager by a king who was no longer his own master.

sanskrit: ayaṃ dhatte veṇur ivātmaghātī; phalaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraḥ dyūtaṃ hi vairāya mahābhayāya; pakvo na budhyaty ayam antakāle
english: This king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, bears fruit like a bamboo that destroys itself by its own fruiting. For dice lead to enmity and great terror; ripe as he is, this man does not understand — at the hour of his end.

sanskrit: nāruṃtudaḥ syān na nṛśaṃsavādī; na hīnataḥ param abhyādadīta yayāsya vācā para udvijeta; na tāṃ vaded ruśatīṃ pāpalokyām
english: One should not be sharp-tongued or speak cruelly; one should not raise oneself above another by belittling them. That stinging speech by which another is made to shudder — one should not speak that burning, sin-destining word.

sanskrit: samuccaranty ativādā hi vaktrād; yair āhataḥ śocati rātryahāni parasya nāmarmasu te patanti; tān paṇḍito nāvasṛjet pareṣu
english: Harsh and excessive words pour out from the mouth; struck by these, another grieves for days and nights. They do not fall upon the vital points of another — yet a wise man would not release such words upon others.

sanskrit: ajo hi śastram akhanat kilaikaḥ; śastre vipanne padbhir apāsya bhūmim nikṛntanaṃ svasya kaṇṭhasya ghoraṃ; tadvad vairaṃ mā khanīḥ pāṇḍuputraiḥ
english: A goat once dug up a weapon for its own use; when the weapon failed, it cast aside the ground with its hooves — that ghastly cutter of its own throat. In like manner, do not dig up enmity with the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: na kiṃ cid īḍyaṃ pravadanti pāpaṃ; vanecaraṃ vā gṛhamedhinaṃ vā tapasvinaṃ saṃparipūrṇavidyaṃ; bhaṣanti haivaṃ śvanarāḥ sadaiva
english: Dogs always bark at those who are praiseworthy — whether the forest-dweller, or the householder, or the ascetic, or the one replete with knowledge — they bark at them as evil.

sanskrit: dvāraṃ sughoraṃ narakasya jihmaṃ; na budhyase dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putra tvām anvetāro bahavaḥ kurūṇāṃ; dyūtodaye saha duḥśāsanena
english: You do not perceive the terrible, crooked gateway to hell, O son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Many of the Kurus will follow you down — together with Duḥśāsana — when this gambling-game reaches its outcome.

sanskrit: majjanty alābūni śilāḥ plavante; muhyanti nāvo 'mbhasi śaśvad eva mūḍho rājā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putro; na me vācaḥ pathyarūpāḥ śṛṇoti
english: Gourds sink while stones float; boats are constantly bewildered upon the water — the foolish king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, does not listen to my words that are wholesome and true.
